facts.statement: Taipei 101 architectural height is 508 m; eight outward-flaring eight-story modules rise above a tapering base.
facts.scope: Overall height and primary organization; not detailed fabrication dimensions.
facts.verification: CTBUH and Skyscraper Museum descriptions agree on 508 m and eight stacked eight-floor units.

facts.statement: The roof is approximately 448 m with a 60 m spire; the small upper tower contains levels 92–100.
facts.scope: Vertical landmarks only; intermediate widths and ornament dimensions estimated from photographs.
facts.verification: Skyscraper Museum identifies 60 m spire and upper levels.

calculations.verification: 508 m × 100 cm/m × 1 px/cm = 50,800 world units. All authored geometry uses centimetres and projection scale 1; no fit-to-page scaling.
448 m ×100 = 44,800 world units; spire rises to 50,800.
